prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: The baseline timing-driven net-weight update caps weights at `max_net_weight` and uses the default `net_weighting_scheme`; switching the update to the "lilith" scheme (momentum-based criticality accumulation) via the shown `TimingOpt.update_net_weights` dispatch will spread weight onto more moderately-critical nets, reducing many moderate violations (TNS) rather than only the worst path (WNS).
Rule-based digest:
total=+0.490 robust(mean-std)=+0.126 min_case=+0.111 all_valid=True
  ariane133-ng45: score=+0.111 dWNS=+13.7% dTNS=+9.2% overflow~103
  bp-ng45: score=+0.182 dWNS=+12.4% dTNS=+22.1% overflow~111
  bp_fe-ng45: score=+0.196 dWNS=+15.4% dTNS=+22.2% overflow~113
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: The hypothesis held: all three cases improved, with dTNS gains (+9.2% to +22.2%) generally exceeding dWNS gains (+12.4% to +15.4%), consistent with lilith spreading weight to moderately-critical nets and reducing many violations rather than only the worst path. All runs valid, no failures. Next step: sweep the lilith momentum/accumulation parameter and `max_net_weight` cap to confirm the TNS-over-WNS tradeoff is tunable and check overflow stays acceptable (~103–113) at higher weight spread.
